title: DSO
summary: Days sales outstanding; how long receivables take to collect.
whyPeCares: PE cares because this KPI gives an early read on growth quality, margin expansion, cash conversion, execution discipline, or exit-story credibility.
goodBadSignals: Good performance shows controlled execution and improving unit economics; bad performance signals leakage, weak process ownership, or a diligence risk requiring deeper segmentation.
improvementActions: Standardize the definition and data owner.
Segment by customer, site, product, team, or channel.
Tie movement to an operating playbook and weekly cadence.

articleSections.title: DSO: The Pulse of Receivables Efficiency
body: In the Private Equity world, Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) is the primary metric we use to measure the efficiency of a company's 'Quote-to-Cash' lifecycle. It quantifies the average number of days it takes to collect payment after a sale has been made. For an Operating Partner, high DSO (e.g., >60 days for a SaaS business) is a red flag signifying poor billing discipline, a lack of collection rigor, or unfavorable credit terms. We view DSO reduction as one of the most reliable 'Quick Wins' for unlocking permanent liquidity and improving the company's net debt position early in the hold period.

The math of DSO is a fundamental working capital ratio: (Average Accounts Receivable) / (Total Credit Sales) * (Number of Days in Period). If a company has $10M in AR and $60M in annual credit sales, its DSO is 60.8 days. For a business with $100M in revenue, every day of DSO reduction releases approximately $274k in cash. We use AR automation tools like Billtrust or YayPay to provide real-time visibility into these figures, moving away from static month-end reports toward a dynamic 'Collections Dashboard' that highlights at-risk accounts before they become past due.

Operating Partners look for 'Structural' DSO improvements by professionalizing the entire credit function. Often, mid-market firms treat collections as a back-office administrative task rather than a strategic financial lever. We instill a 'Cash Culture' where every sales rep and account manager understands that a deal isn't truly 'Closed' until the cash is in the bank. By implementing automated 'Dunning' workflows and incentivizing early payments, we can often shave 10-15 days off the DSO in the first 100 days of the investment. This 'Found Money' is a direct driver of MOIC.
articleSections.callout: DSO is the scoreboard of your billing discipline; if it's high, you're effectively acting as an interest-free bank for your customers.

articleSections.title: The Aging Bucket Audit: Identifying Chronic Offenders
body: To drive sustainable DSO reduction, you must move beyond the 'Average' and perform a deep-dive audit of your 'Aging Buckets' (0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91+ days). Senior Operating Partners look for 'Chronic Offenders'—customers who consistently pay outside of their negotiated terms. We use tools like Quadient AR (formerly YayPay) to automate this analysis and identify the 'Root Causes' of late payments. Is it a dispute over the invoice? A lack of 'Autopay' options? Or simply a customer who has been 'trained' that we won't follow up for 60 days? Identifying these patterns is the first step toward clinical collection.

The math of the aging audit reveals the 'Opportunity Cost' of poor collections. We calculate the 'Interest Expense' on our past-due receivables using our current cost of debt (e.g., 10%). If we have $5M in the 91+ bucket, that is costing the firm $500k a year in interest alone. Armed with this data, we can move high-risk customers to 'Pre-payment' or 'Credit Card' models, eliminating the DSO risk entirely for those segments. We also look for 'Dispute Density'—the percentage of invoices that are contested—as a signal of underlying service or product quality issues.

We implement 'SLA-Based' collections where the intensity of the follow-up increases as the invoice ages. Day 1: Automated friendly reminder. Day 15: SDR follow-up. Day 30: Account Executive intervention. Day 60: Legal notice. By professionalizing this 'Escalation Ladder,' we reduce the 'Time to Payment' and improve the overall predictability of our cash flow. Operating Partners use this discipline to 'Harden' the balance sheet and ensure that the business remains a high-velocity, cash-generative machine that is ready for the next level of growth.

articleSections.title: Billing Discipline and the 'Quote-to-Cash' Friction
body: High DSO is often a symptom of 'Friction' in the billing process rather than a customer's inability to pay. If an invoice is inaccurate, sent to the wrong person, or arrives 30 days late, the customer has a valid excuse to delay payment. We prioritize 'Billing Integrity' by implementing CPQ (Configure, Price, Quote) tools like Salesforce CPQ to ensure that what was sold is exactly what is invoiced. By automating the handoff from 'Closed Won' to 'Invoice Sent,' we can often reduce the 'Billing Cycle' by 3-5 days, which translates directly into lower DSO.

The math of billing friction is measured through the 'Error Rate' and 'Re-issue Frequency.' If 10% of your invoices require a credit note and a re-issue, you are effectively adding 15-20 days to the DSO for those accounts. We use tools like Billtrust to move toward 'Electronic Invoicing' and 'Integrated Payment Portals,' allowing customers to pay with a single click. By making it 'Easy to Pay,' we remove the psychological and administrative barriers that lead to late payments. This 'Self-Service' approach also lowers our internal AR overhead.

Operating Partners also review 'Standard Payment Terms' across the customer base. Many founder-led firms grant 'Net 60' or 'Net 90' terms without realizing the mathematical impact on their enterprise value. We work to standardize the portfolio on 'Net 30' or 'Net 15,' and we implement 'Late Fees' that are actually enforced. For customers who insist on longer terms, we price-in a 'Terms Premium' to compensate for the higher working capital requirement. By treating payment terms as a 'Pricing' lever, we protect the margin and the balance sheet simultaneously.

articleSections.title: Incentive Alignment: Making Cash a Sales Metric
body: One of the most effective ways to drive DSO reduction is to align sales incentives with cash collection. We move the sales organization away from 'Bonus on Booking' toward 'Bonus on Cash Receipt.' When a sales rep's commission is held until the customer pays the invoice, their behavior changes overnight. They become highly selective about the 'Credit Quality' of their prospects and proactively help the collections team clear up any billing disputes. This 'Alignment' ensures that the front line is protecting the balance sheet as much as the top line.

The math of incentive alignment is measured through 'Commission Accruals.' We track the 'Average Days to Commission Payment' to see how well the sales team is managing their accounts. We also implement 'Clawback' provisions where a rep must return their commission if an account becomes more than 120 days past due. This ensures that we aren't 'Buying' growth at the expense of terminal value. Operating Partners use this discipline to build a 'Professional' sales force that understands the full 'Economic Value' of the deal, not just the contract sign-off.

We also provide the sales team with 'Visibility' into their customers' payment status using Salesforce integrations. A rep should never be surprised by a 'Credit Hold' when they are trying to close an upsell. By giving them real-time access to the AR data, they can handle collections as part of their regular account management cadence. This 'Multi-threaded' approach to collections is far more effective than a standalone AR team and results in a structurally lower DSO. When Sales and Finance are working toward the same 'Cash Target,' the business becomes an unstoppable liquidity engine.

articleSections.title: Exit Readiness: Defending the 'Cash Quality' of the Asset
body: As we approach the exit, the DSO ratio is the primary tool we use to prove the asset's 'Operational Discipline' to potential buyers. A buyer will be highly skeptical of an EBITDA figure that isn't backed by actual cash flow. We prepare for this by performing a 'Sell-Side Working Capital Audit' 12 months out, creating a 'DSO Bridge' that shows how we've improved collections through automation and term standardization. We use Billtrust data to provide a 'Clean Data' trail that proves our DSO is sustainable and free of 'One-time' noise.

Buyers pay a premium for 'High-Quality Receivables.' If we can show that 95%+ of our AR is in the 0-30 day bucket, we prove that our customer base is high-quality and our billing engine is world-class. We highlight our 'Low Bad Debt' write-offs and 'High Autopay' adoption as proof of our management rigor. By de-risking the 'Receivables' portion of the balance sheet, we justify a higher revenue multiple and ensure a smooth 'Net Working Capital' (NWC) settlement at close. We position the asset as a 'Low-Risk' cash machine.

The final act is the 'NWC Target' negotiation. By driving DSO to an industry-low level *before* we go to market, we set a favorable baseline for the working capital peg. This ensures that we don't 'give back' value during the closing process. We use historical data to show the buyer exactly how the 'Cash Windfall' we've unlocked is permanent and scalable. By delivering a 'Hardened' balance sheet, we maximize the exit price and deliver a superior return to our LPs. In the end, a controlled and improving DSO is the ultimate proof of an Operating Partner's success.
